FD-B12 validates complete accepted NA-A1 source-key presence before semantic status evaluation, including explicit-null fields such as night_audit_run_id, attempt_number, started_by, source_fingerprint, and property_id. Missing keys are not equivalent to explicit null values and fail closed with FD_B12_INVALID_NIGHT_AUDIT_LOCK_PROJECTION. Active Night Audit evidence now requires a strict positive integer attempt_number with no coercion. Gate 7 exposes the exact whitelist gate, owner, satisfied, detail, status, source_status, close_lock_active, business_date, property_timezone, attempt_number, run_status, started_at, evidence_unavailable_codes, evaluated_at, and source_fingerprint, while omitting raw night_audit_run_id, started_by, property_id, and property_business_date_id. NIGHT_AUDIT_LOCK_CLEAR satisfies only the Night Audit gate with null attempt and started_at; NIGHT_AUDIT_LOCK_ACTIVE blocks with NIGHT_AUDIT_CLOSE_LOCK_ACTIVE while preserving active attempt and started_at; unavailable source evidence remains fail-closed with NIGHT_AUDIT_LOCK_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE and null Gate 7 attempt/started_at. Queue minimization remains unchanged, authorization-first behavior remains unchanged, checkout execution remains unauthorized, can_execute=false, and the projection remains zero-mutation across Front Desk, Guest Ledger, General Cashier, Business Date, Night Audit, folio, settlement, close, advance, reopen, checkpoints, and posting state. provenance.note: NA-A2 savepoint-capability correction measurement: 2 exact PostgreSQL classes / 20 tests / 914 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors. The earlier exact-object, non-null PostgreSQL backend PID, and txid_current transaction ID proof remains. After the Property and Business Date locks and transaction proof are validated, the service generates cryptographically random capability evidence and installs it through parameterized set_config with transaction-local scope; only its SHA-256 hash is retained in the static WeakMap. Validation occurs before any night_audit_runs query: one PostgreSQL query resolves backend PID, transaction ID, and current transaction-local capability state, then hash_equals verifies the private issuance evidence together with all authoritative identities. Nested rollback proves the retained exact PHP context object has the same backend PID and same outer transaction ID while PostgreSQL reverts the capability state; the guard rejects it with NA_A2_INVALID_OPERATIONAL_LOCK_CONTEXT before any Night Audit query and all tracked tables remain write-free. Successful nested savepoint release preserves the capability and repeated outer-transaction attestations keep a deterministic fingerprint. Same-transaction repeated attestations keep a deterministic fingerprint. A second successful acquisition replaces the transaction capability: the newest context succeeds and the prior context is rejected before Night Audit query, enforcing one active NA-A2 capability per transaction and preventing cross-Property reuse. The generated capability value is absent from the public lock context, toArray output, Night Audit attestation, source fingerprints, logs, and error messages. A stale issued context remains rejected on the same backend in a new transaction, and a manually constructed but unissued context remains rejected. Database proof failures fail closed with the previous database exception retained as cause. Real PostgreSQL concurrency proof continues through separate PHP processes with distinct PostgreSQL backend PIDs, Property-scoped locking, finite worker timeout and cleanup. No migration, route, controller, permission, confirmation intent, checkout command, checkout UI, checkout runtime, or checkout execution is added; can_execute=false and checkout remains unauthorized.
